Subject: Vanguard Health — VPC & compliance discovery (recap)

Hi Alex / Sara,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the clear framing on regulatory constraints. Quick recap from our side and the immediate asks we left with: 

Summary of drivers (what you told us)
- Regulatory/data residency: primary requirement is that inference compute and short-term KV/cache must run inside Vanguard’s VPC in us-east-1. No user PII may leave the VPC.
- Air-gap/archive: backups and long-term model artifacts should be writable to an air-gapped archive managed by Vanguard; Redwood should support export-only flow.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) required; HSM integration for key lifecycle is preferred.
- Evidence: Procurement/legal asked for SOC 2 scope, data retention policy, and audit log samples.

Goals and success criteria
- POC timeline: target 6–10 weeks from SOW sign.
- Performance: support 5 RPS sustained for chat endpoints with 300–400ms p95 latency for prompt lengths ~512 tokens.
- Security: no persistent token storage outside customer-managed volume; full auditability and request tracing.

Network and ops blockers we noted
- Network: Vanguard netops requires static egress IPs or routed private peering (ExpressRoute/Direct Connect equivalent).
- Firewall rules: need list of destination CIDRs for our control plane and telemetry endpoints; outbound-only flow preferred.
- DNS & routing: explicit NAT/Gateway mapping; we cannot assume outbound IP translation without confirmation.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) I’ll send the Vanguard discovery checklist (attached) with fields for your network team to fill (static IPs, allowed ports, proxy).
2) We’ll produce a short MOP and example PoC plan for on-prem/VPC integration — first draft by EOD Monday.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your network/security engineers — proposed slots next week (I’ll follow with a Doodle).

Deliverables attached: Vanguard-Discovery-Checklist.pdf (networking + compliance fields).

If I missed anything critical from today’s call, flag it and I’ll update the docs.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference – Developer-first inference platform

Dev — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct: compute must run in our VPC; we will not allow persistent storage of PII outside our tenancy. Short-term caches are ok as long as they are ephemeral and never written to object storage under your account.
- KMS: must be customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMKs). We may have to run a KMS proxy for on-prem deployments; we’ll confirm with cloud security.
- Air-gap: acceptable approach is pull-only archival of logs/artifacts to a vault we control; Redwood must provide export tooling and attestations.

Procurement note (cc’d): we’ll expect SOC 2 Type II report, a simplified data flow diagram, and a template SOW for a VPC-only deployment. Procurement will start an initial review next week.

A couple of asks for your deliverable set:
1) Include an example network ACL + firewall rule template (ports/protocols) so our infra can pre-authorize.
2) Confirm whether Redwood’s control plane needs any inbound connectivity from our VPC, or if all control-plane traffic can be outbound-only.

We’re targeting a decision window in ~8–10 weeks, but that’s contingent on procurement turn. Happy to take your PoC plan and MOP. When you send proposed tech-dive times, please include our security lead (I’ll confirm the name tomorrow).

—Alex
Alex Grant
Director, Cloud Security | Vanguard Health
alex.grant@vanguard-health.com
